text:
mina: Quick heads-up — I ran a small bring-up of a hybrid AWQ+FP8 profile on 7B-rev2 with our prefix KV cache + continuous batching. Findings: accuracy delta ~-0.9% (vs fp16 baseline) on conversational-eval-v2 (1k), p95 latency +30% at 512 tokens, throughput roughly the same.

sam: Can you paste the config and the eval snippet?

mina: Config pasted below. note the main knobs: prefetch=true, batch.coalesce_ms=6, quant_profile=awq_fp8_hybrid, fallback=int8_gptq

```
# experiment config
model: 7b-rev2
quant_profile:
  type: awq_fp8_hybrid
  per_channel: true
batching:
  continuous: true
  coalesce_ms: 6
prefetch:
  enabled: true
  policy: prefix_kv
routing:
  fallback: int8_gptq
```

mina: Eval snippet: EM 62.4 -> 61.4, Rouge-L 46.2 -> 45.5, avg perplexity +4.1%. I ran 3 seeds, stdev ~0.15 on EM.

toni: Interesting. Did you control for cache staleness? prefix_kv with prefetch + continuous batching can return slightly stale KV if a request hits a different quant variant mid-stream. Could be quality churn.

mina: I thought about that — logs show a few requests where routing switched to fallback mid-session (CPU fallbacks under load). Example log: 

```
[2024-11-08T14:02:21Z] request_id=xy123 route=awq_fp8_hybrid -> fallback=int8_gptq (capacity spike)
[2024-11-08T14:02:21Z] kvcache: prefix_key=conv:abc123 hit=true variant=awq_fp8_hybrid
[2024-11-08T14:02:21Z] model_switch: int8_gptq applied, kv_state_mismatch=true
```

mina: When model_switch happened, we see generation artifacts (repeats, off-by-one tokens) consistent with KV mismatch.

sam: Could the quantized variants have incompatible KV layouts? AWQ FP8 uses different kv dtype/packing than GPTQ int8. If the runtime assumes compatible KV layout for prefix cache, that would create corruption.

mina: Exactly the hypothesis. I checked kernel metadata — AWQ stores k/v in float16 reframed layout; GPTQ int8 uses packed int8 + dequant table. Our prefix cache currently stores opaque bytes and assumes per-arch reader can adapt, but it doesn't.

toni: Repro steps? Easy to test: force routing to same variant (no fallback) during eval to see if delta goes away. Also test prefetch=false to confirm prefetch churn is the amplifier.

mina: Did both: 1) pinned routing to awq_fp8_hybrid (no fallback) -> EM drop reduced to -0.2%, latency stable. 2) prefetch=false (still allow fallback) -> EM drop -0.7. 3) pinned to int8_gptq -> EM -0.6. So looks like the major hit is when switching mid-session.

eva: Good isolation. Suggest adding a cache-variant-tag in prefix keys (e.g., conv:variant:sessionid) so mismatches never read wrong layout. Minimal change: append quant hash to prefix key.

sam: We should also add detection: when model_switch occurs, invalidate prefix KV for that session and emit metric kv_mismatch_count.

mina: Agreed. Created a quick patch in a personal branch that appends quant_hash to key and invalidates on switch. Ran 1000-sample smoke: EM delta back to -0.1 and KV mismatch metrics drop to 0.

ci-bot: Deploy pipeline kicked off for branch mina/kv-quant-tag (canary to eu-west). CI tests: unit kv key, integration small-run.

toni: Action items:
- mina: open PR & add migration notes for cache key format (must tolerate both keys in read path for 7 days)
- eng-runtime: add kv_mismatch metric + alert if >10/min
- eval: run full 10k conversational-eval-v2 with pinned routing + pinned prefetch=false and with new key tagging

mina: I'll open PR and schedule the eval. Expecting canary data in ~2h. If canary good, we'll roll patch across dedicated pools and then offer a migration window for private deploys.

sam: Nice catch. This explains why continuous batching exacerbated it — coalesced requests meant more chance to hit mixed routing before session-level reconciliation.

mina: Short-term mitigation: reduce batch.coalesce_ms to 2ms and disable prefetch for critical SLAs. Longer term: key-tag + mismatch detection.

ci-bot: Canary deploy succeeded in eu-west. smoke eval job started.

mina: I'll post results once smoke finishes. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
